correctness.rationale: For any Noetherian non-UFD domain \(A\), Hilbert's basis theorem makes \(A[X]\) Noetherian, hence ACCP and atomic. Nonunique factorizations in \(A\) remain nonunique in \(A[X]\) because factors of a nonzero constant must have degree zero and polynomial units over a domain are constant units. The identity companion \(h(F)=F\) is completely multiplicative and the formal product rule gives \(D_X(FG)=D_X(F)h(G)+D_X(G)h(F)\), while \(D_X(X)=1\). For the explicit ring, the norm \(a^2+5b^2\) proves the displayed irreducibles and units. The packaged exact checker independently replays the explicit norm and polynomial-product identities on a finite regression family.

originality.rationale: The focal 2020 paper explicitly asks whether any non-UFD factorization domain admits a nonzero L-additive function. Its cited 2013 predecessor concerns the stronger factorization-normalized arithmetic derivative and proves negative results for quadratic integer rings; the 2024 Emmons--Xiao paper repeats that stronger obstruction while pursuing number-field extensions. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches did not locate the polynomial-ring formal-derivative construction or a statement implying it.

value.rationale: The theorem directly answers a published existence question and does so for an infinite structural class rather than one isolated example. It also cleanly separates two notions that the nearby literature can make easy to conflate: arbitrary L-additivity versus the stronger arithmetic-derivative normalization on irreducibles. The proof is elementary but mathematically substantive because it closes the stated existence gap with a reusable construction.
